_comment: One verdict per fleet-wide hand-fix id (an id in 10 or more connector ledgers), settled against a press release. retire: the press generates the behavior from retire_at on; check_handfixes.py stops demanding the entry on a connector recorded at or above retire_at and demands native_asserts instead, and replay_handfixes.py removes the stale entry and runs the gates. replay: replay_handfixes.py re-applies it after every reprint with the named recipe. delegated: another tool owns it. keep_manual names connectors where the shared id carries a connector-specific part a person must reconcile. floors: minimum module versions every print at or above applies_from must resolve. See docs/reprint-survival.md.

interim-http-security-note-2026-10-22.reason: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.
interim-http-security-note-2026-10-22.proof: Raw 4.34.0 ninjaone-mcp: --transport http with no token exits with '<PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN must be set'; no bearer 401, wrong bearer 401; --addr 0.0.0.0 without --tls-cert refuses. Same properties on cipp, servosity and ninjaone in the 2026-10-23 press 4.34.0 method probe, section 2. 62 of 65 raw 4.34.0 renders declare httpTokenEnvVar; the other 3 (connectwise-automate, levelio, n-central) serve stdio only.

keep_manual.cipp: The entry also pins SKILL.md '## Read this first: some CIPP GET calls change things', which stays true after the reprint (the GET endpoints still mutate; 4.34.0 only gates them). Move that assert to its own entry, then remove this one.

doctor-verdict-tracks-reality.reason: Press 4.34.0 took part of the fix (placeholder refusal, info keys) but doctor still prints 'present, not verified' instead of probing the credential, calls a 404 at / 'reachable', and never names the base-URL variable.
doctor-verdict-tracks-reality.proof: check_doctor_truth.py on raw 4.34.0 ninjaone, hudu and connectwise-rmm: FAIL (healthy: 'present, not verified'; wrong-base: 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)'; placeholder never names <PREFIX>_BASE_URL). Same three on main: PASS. 21 of 65 renders already probe credentials (verify_path); the recipe edits only where the generated suggestion block exists and the gate decides.
doctor-verdict-tracks-reality.upstream: cli-printing-press: doctor probes no credential when auth.verify_path is absent, reads a 404 at / as reachable, and never names <PREFIX>_BASE_URL (drafted 2026-10-23, not filed)

install-credentials-declared-on-every-ch.proof: Raw 4.34.0 ninjaone manifest.json server.mcp_config.env: 2 keys; main: 6 (BASE_URL, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, NO_CONFIG_WRITE, OAUTH_SCOPE, TOKEN_URL).

token-request-stays-on-origin.reason: Press 4.34.0 routes every token request through the same-origin token client (the hand-fix's two redirect tests pass on it), but compares hosts with strings.EqualFold: an IPv6 zone that differs only in case, and a host that only Unicode case folding equates, count as the same origin.
token-request-stays-on-origin.proof: Hand-fix tests on raw 4.34.0 ninjaone: TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin PASS; TestOAuthTokenSameOriginComparesHostsLikeTheNetwork FAILS on fe80::1%lan0 vs %LAN0 and on k vs U+212A. On raw 4.24.0 both redirect tests FAIL.
token-request-stays-on-origin.upstream: cli-printing-press: the token client's same-origin check folds Unicode and IPv6 zone case (drafted 2026-10-23, not filed)

env-oauth-secrets-not-persisted.reason: Press 4.34.0 keeps the environment markers through SaveTokens and generates MarkCredentialsExplicit, so a client ID or secret read from the environment is never written by a token save.
env-oauth-secrets-not-persisted.proof: Proof test (env client ID and secret set, Load, SaveTokens, then every file under the temporary config home searched): raw 4.24.0 ninjaone FAIL (the secret lands in config.toml); main PASS; raw 4.34.0 PASS, with the control (the minted token was written) holding in each.

sync-skips-withheld-row.reason: Press 4.35.1 aborts a whole batch, and with it the resource's sync, when the credential kit's SQLite driver withholds one row (#612: hubspot-calls-crm stopped at one row). The press has no withheld-row notion; the recipe skips the row, keeps the batch and the walk, and ends the resource stored with the row ids named (stderr, a sync_warning rows_withheld event, the summary's "withheld") and its watermark kept. synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row is never fatal; before, the resource ended failed and the run exited 1, so mcp2 never marked hubspot synced.
sync-skips-withheld-row.proof: store/withheld_test.go TestUpsertBatchSkipsWithheldRow in every carrier; zammad and hubspot adopter syncs with one row carrying the CLI's own token (.review/adopter-proof.md). synccpu: zammad first sync against the #612 fake vendor with a declared password in user 101 exits 0, stores 999 of 1,000 users, names 101 on stderr and in the summary, and no file carries the value (credential-kit/synccpu-report.md).
sync-skips-withheld-row.upstream: none: the kit is downstream of the press

keep_manual.dnsfilter: upsertResourceBatch returns the stored ids too (sync-seen-ids-are-stored-ids): the batch's withheld return and the page's pageWithheld block are wired by hand, and UpsertBatchStoredIDs keeps the stored ids when the error is a withheld row.
keep_manual.superops: sync walks GraphQL pages through db.UpsertBatch, not upsertResourceBatch: the pageWithheld block, the empty-page guard and the stored end (a withheld row is never fatal) are wired by hand in syncResource; superops_held_record_test.go and superops_held_sinks_test.go assert the skip-the-row contract.

sync-event-writer-serialized.reason: Press 4.24.0 to 4.34.2 sync gives every --concurrency worker of its top-level pool the same writer (syncEventWriter, cmd.OutOrStdout() or in machine output cmd.ErrOrStderr()) and nothing serializes Write. os.Stdout tolerates that; the --deliver mirror (a bytes.Buffer) and the --receipt-file / --audit-dir capture (a running SHA-256) do not, so a sync with --concurrency above 1 can panic in bytes.Buffer.grow (seen on Windows CI, PR #655) or write a receipt whose hash does not match the output. Only the dependent-resource path wraps its writer (lockedWriter).
sync-event-writer-serialized.proof: go test -race ./internal/cli on veeam: 28 races before the fix, 0 after. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites (four workers, --dry-run, machine and human output) fails before the recipe and passes after on veeam (4.24.0), abnormal (4.34.2, machine-format branch) and warranty (4.34.2, per-resource tier routing); see the PR that added this record.

entry.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
entry.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
entry.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

sync-event-writer-serialized.upstream: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369 (filed): sync's top-level worker pool shares an unserialized event writer

limiter-ramps-only-while-pacing.reason: Press 4.35.1's AdaptiveLimiter multiplies its rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling on a server that sends no rate-limit headers (HubSpot sends X-HubSpot-RateLimit-*, which ParseRateLimitHeaders does not read). mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 after about 2,500 requests, and from there a 429's halving could not slow a single request. The recipe raises the rate only while the last Wait slept, so the rate stays near what the requests reach.
limiter-ramps-only-while-pacing.proof: cliutil TestAdaptiveLimiter_RampsUpAfterSuccesses (extended): 50 successes with no Wait pacing leave the rate at 2; fails without the guard (ramped to 6.1), passes with it, on hubspot and zammad.
limiter-ramps-only-while-pacing.upstream: none filed yet: the press template's blind ramp has no ceiling (synccpu report)

sync-progress-measured-rate.reason: Press 4.35.1's sync prints c.RateLimit(), the adaptive limiter's current ceiling, as sync_progress rate_rps and as [x req/s] on the human line. That is the most the limiter would allow, not what the sync did: mcp2 read 4.9 while storing about 33 rows a second (#694). The recipe measures the rows the walk stored over a recent 30 s window, reports it as rows_per_sec, keeps rate_rps as the same measured value, and names the ceiling limiter_ceiling_rps.
sync-progress-measured-rate.proof: TestSyncProgressReportsMeasuredRowsNotTheLimiter walks real resources against a fake client whose limiter reads 4.9 and fails on the old event (no rows_per_sec) and when the helper is handed the ceiling; syncfix report has the before and after on real binaries.

entry.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
entry.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
entry.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

sync-forbidden-not-partial.reason: Press 4.35.1's sync leaves a resource the vendor refuses (HTTP 403) at last_attempt_complete = 0, and mcpStoreStatus calls any such row partial, so store_status can never leave partial on a token with a narrower scope (#692: zammad overviews and tags, hubspot imports). The recipe records the refusal in its own table, clears it as each attempt starts, and reports complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished. last_attempt_complete keeps its 0 and 1 meaning, because hand-written commands read it that way.
sync-forbidden-not-partial.proof: TestSyncForbiddenResourceIsSkippedThenReattempted and TestStoreStatusSeparatesForbiddenFromBroken in every carrier; both fail if the mark or the attempt-start clear is removed. syncfix report has the before and after on real binaries.

entry.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
entry.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
entry.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

sync-progress-throttled.reason: Press 4.35.1's sync writes one sync_progress line per page, and every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check of the write plus the stream's tail, whatever its size. At HubSpot's 10 rows a page and the 3.3 pages a second seen on mcp2, that check was 74% of sync's CPU on linux/arm64 (#696, syncprobe report). The recipe lets each resource's walk write its first page's line and then at most one every 5 seconds; the line still carries the measured rate, and sync_complete and the human done line keep the final count. Every line written is still checked.
sync-progress-throttled.proof: TestSyncWritesProgressAtMostOncePerInterval walks a default resource that reads three pages from a fake and fails when more than the first page's line is written inside one interval, or when sync_complete loses the final count; TestSyncProgressDueOncePerInterval fails on a guard that never records the interval, never reports, or compares the wrong way. syncfix report (syncfix2) has the CPU before and after on hubspot and zammad.

entry.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
entry.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
